page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for hardware-accelerated vector and matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1714.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2251.0. Memory bandwidth is also a bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 19.35 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 12.78 GB/sec. Text processing and single-threaded compression perform at average levels, whereas software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations show weaker throughput.

The n4-standard-2 represents a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require high memory density or intensive parallel processing. Its hardware profile is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale background tasks. The lack of local storage and low multi-core efficiency make it less suitable for heavy database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or parallelized build pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an entry-level general-purpose instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM on an x86_64 Intel architecture with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. This instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0, but reveal limitations in multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, with large-block memory read speeds of 19.35 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the n4-standard-2 offers a cost-effective profile for low-intensity, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight background processes, while showing performance trade-offs in data-intensive or highly parallelized workloads.
